GROWW.why: Roughly doubled since the ₹100 IPO. Growth drivers: transacting users up 25% to over 2 crore, cash-equity market share up to 28.8% from 21.6%, derivatives share 18.1%, SIP inflows up 32% against 16% for the industry, plus lending, commodities and wealth products. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 66% to ₹1,501 crore and profit rose 94% to ₹735 crore. Q3 FY26 profit fell 28% on a one-time gain a year earlier.
GROWW.outlook: Motilal Oswal initiated Buy at ₹185 (the price has since passed it), arguing demat penetration is only about 14% against about 62% in the US. Risks: valuation above global brokers like Robinhood and Interactive Brokers, income that moves with market activity, new sign-ups slowing as IPO and ETF activity cooled, and tighter risk controls.

PINELABS.why: Below the ₹221 IPO price: it fell about 36% in 2026 to mid-June and dropped as much as 5.6% after Q1 FY27 when profit fell 67% quarter on quarter despite 20% revenue growth, because one-time investments in cloud, network and enterprise sales squeezed margins. Cited too: stretched valuation at IPO (about ₹25,000 crore for a recent loss-maker), lock-in expiry selling and a risk-off March.
PINELABS.outlook: It turned profitable in FY26 (profit ₹113 crore against a ₹145 crore loss), with operating margin up to 13% and gross cash of ₹2,732 crore against ₹283 crore borrowings. Morgan Stanley is Equal-weight with a ₹245 target. Management says margins should recover as one-time costs fade; consistent quarterly profit is the test.

EMMVEE.why: Up about 49% over a year on guidance and expansion: management expects EBITDA of ₹2,200-2,400 crore in FY27 rising to ₹3,000 crore in FY28, with a 6 GW TOPCon expansion and a 9 GW cell backward-integration plan. Jefferies initiated Buy at ₹440 on 20 August 2026. FY26 revenue was reported at about ₹2,360 crore with profit near ₹369 crore.
EMMVEE.outlook: The expansion is about ₹5,500 crore, about 60% debt-funded, so leverage is the watch item. Valuation figures differ widely by source (P/E 18 to 143) and the price sits near its 52-week high (₹371). Promoters hold about 80%.

PHYSICS.why: Slightly above the IPO price after a rough start (a 14% drop within three sessions in January 2026). Revenue grew 35% to ₹3,899 crore for FY26 with offline centres at 45% of revenue, and losses narrowed sharply (Q4 FY26 loss about ₹69-74 crore against ₹293 crore). The shares rose about 5% on 28 May 2026 on the narrower loss.
PHYSICS.outlook: Early FY27 sales are up 36% year on year per the founders and brokerages see growth potential, but whether profitability holds is unproven. Q4 loss figures varied across sources (₹69 to ₹132 crore), so verify in the filing. Q1 FY27 results were not found.

UTLSOLAR.why: The stock went from about ₹191 in March 2026 to about ₹435 in September on Q4 FY26 results: profit up 107.5% and quarterly revenue up 87.5% (FY26 revenue ₹2,654 crore, up 72%), plus a solar cell manufacturing investment. Motilal Oswal points to rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar, its 1 GW domestic-content cell facility and a planned 1.2 GW TOPCon expansion.
UTLSOLAR.outlook: Motilal Oswal is Buy with a ₹470 target. Valuation is full (trailing P/E about 37) and only about 10% of shares are in public hands, with insiders at about 90%, which can exaggerate price swings. Results after May 2026 were not found.

CAPILLARY.why: Below the ₹577 IPO price (it listed at a 3% discount). One report blames AI-disruption fears and a muted December quarter for a roughly 35% fall from the peak. Nine-month revenue to December 2025 rose 22% to ₹543 crore while Q3 profit fell 20% to ₹8 crore. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% to ₹256.6 crore but an exceptional loss of ₹33.4 crore pushed reported profit negative (normalised profit ₹25.4 crore).
CAPILLARY.outlook: Growth levers: AI-driven loyalty software and a deal for Mastercard's SessionM (about $35 million of annual recurring revenue, over 40 enterprise clients). No formal revenue guidance was found. The open question is whether AI is hurting the core business or just sentiment. Reported FY26 revenue differed between sources.

EXCELSOFT.why: Down about 43% over a year (52-week range ₹66-143). Explanations are weak: a promotional blog cites foreign selling and de-rating, MarketsMojo cites stretched valuation, no near-term catalyst and a downgrade, and standalone profit fell about 44% quarter on quarter in the June 2026 quarter. This is the most company-specific negative data point found.
EXCELSOFT.outlook: No company guidance or analyst forecast was found. It is a vertical SaaS firm in learning and assessment. Treat as unresearched beyond price data until it files fuller commentary.

MEESHO.why: About double the ₹111 IPO price after a spike and a pullback. Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% to ₹3,531 crore, order value 43%, and the loss narrowed 88% to about ₹166 crore, lifting the shares 8% in May. Contribution margin reached 4% of order value on lower logistics costs; transacting sellers passed 1.04 million (+81%). Jefferies set ₹240 and the shares rose about 6% on 6 October 2026.
MEESHO.outlook: Jefferies expects about 25% annual order-value growth for five years (15% more users and similar order frequency, less a 5% fall in average order value). Targets range from JM Financial's ₹170 Reduce (January) to ₹260 from another broker; Choice says upside is priced in. Still EBITDA-loss-making (FY26) and valuation is the debate.

AMAGI.why: Up about 66% over a year. Revenue grew roughly 30% (about 29.5% in FY26) as media clients move from hardware to cloud infrastructure and ad impressions rise. A July 2026 note shows analysts lifting their target to ₹690 from ₹625 on better growth and margins; a head of sales for German-speaking and Central/Eastern Europe was hired. Profit softened in the August board update and the shares dipped 3.4%.
AMAGI.outlook: Management expects SaaS-like gross margins, though revenue recognition timing is a challenge. Valuation is the main risk: price-to-book was about 25x against a 3.2x peer median in March 2026, trailing earnings were negative and Simply Wall St scores valuation 1 of 6. No consolidated 2026 earnings forecast was found.
